deploy-bot: Deploy started for release `v3.12.0` -> canary 10% -> rollout window 30m. ops/rollout runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploy-watchdog :rocket:
olivia (oncall): tagging SLO dashboard and eyeballing p95 & 5xx. can someone pin the previous model variant in case we need fast fallback? :eyes:
raj (platform): pinned model variant `embed-v2@2026-03-12` in router config. command I ran: `rdwctl pin variant embed-route --variant embed-v2@2026-03-12`
maria (releases): noted in release notes. canary rollout 10% scheduled to 30% at +10m if healthy.
tony (sre): seeing a 5m uptick in request errors on the canary group, small but rising. p50 stable, p95 +120ms, 5xx from 0.2% -> 1.8% in last 3m.
slo-bot: ALERT: ml_inference_5xx_rate (canary) crossed warning threshold (0.8%). current: 1.82% | window: 5m | triggered_at: 5498765440
olivia (oncall): paste the query that shows the 5xx spike? want to correlate with prefix-cache GC job.
tony (sre): query: ```
sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="embed-canary",code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="embed-canary"}[5m])) * 100
```
olivia (oncall): thanks. overlaying infra events — there was a prefix-cache GC at 5498765380 on a subset of hosts. might be related.
raj (platform): rolling back cache config temporarily on canary hosts: `rdw infra set cache.gc.enabled=false --scope canary`
maria (releases): do we pause traffic shift to 30% for now?
ton y (sre): typo in name — correcting: tony (sre): yes, pause. i'll set canary weight to 10% -> hold.
deploy-bot: Runbook command: `deploy-bot pause-rollout 5498765432`
olivia (oncall): deploy-bot pause-rollout executed by olivia. :white_check_mark: Why did the error rate spike for POST /embed? traces show increased backend 503 from worker 7.
ton y (sre): tony (sre): worker 7 had OOM kill during GC sweep, logs: ```
[5498765382] OOM killer invoked: pid 24861 (embed-worker)
[5498765383] oom_reaper: reaped process 24861
```
raj (platform): reassigning canary traffic away from worker 7 hosts: `rdwctl route update --exclude-host host-7a,host-7b --route embed-canary`
olivia (oncall): good. also flagging a regression ticket: INF-4832 with traces + sample requests.
maria (releases): updating release notes with pause + incident link INF-4832, marking this rollout as paused for triage.
ton y (sre): propose we do a quick canary patch: disable heavy GC path and restart workers on the affected hosts, then slowly ramp if 5xx returns <0.5% for 10m. anyone object?
raj (platform): agree. I'll prepare a hotfix bundle `v3.12.0-hotfix-1` with GC guard.
slo-bot: INFO: When paused, routing will keep canary at 10% until manual resume. Reminder: automated rollback triggers at 5xx >= 3% for 5m.
olivia (oncall): timeline: pause at 5498765445, hotfix ready ETA ~12m, restart + monitor 10m, decision point at ~5498766145.
ton y (sre): I'll own post-restart smoke: will run these quick checks: `curl -sS -I https://embed.canary/health` and a sample batch of 100 requests via `locust` script.
maria (releases): pinging product + cs for potential impact comms.
raj (platform): rolling host restarts now (controlled): `rdw infra restart host-7a host-7b --reason "OOM GC hotfix"`
slo-bot: METRIC: ml_inference_latency_p95 (canary) back to baseline after restart? current p95=310ms (pre-spike 290ms). 5xx now sampling down to 0.6%.
ton y (sre): initial smoke looks good: health OK, 5xx stabilizing. continue monitoring.
olivia (oncall): keeping the pause. if stable at 0.5% for 10m, we can consider resuming to 30% with gradual 5% increments.
maria (releases): documenting decision in the release thread and adding rollback playbook steps in the ticket. :memo:
raj (platform): once we resume, let's enable extra traces on canary for another 30m. `rdwctl trace enable --route embed-canary --duration 30m`
deploy-bot: Reminder: automatic rollback window remains active until manual resume. Please mark thread when you resume: `deploy-bot resume-rollout 5498765432`
olivia (oncall): will post resume timestamp. thanks everyone. :pray:
ton y (sre): tony (sre): follow-up: created postmortem stub at https://redwood.internal/infra/INF-4832/postmortem for details.
-- end of thread --
